documents.title: Introduction to Programming Languages and Compilers

key_facts.fact: Programming languages are notations for describing computations to people and to machines.

Programming domains mentioned in this material include Scientific Applications (Fortran, ALGOL 60, Julia, MATLAB), Business Applications (COBOL, DATABUS, PL/B), Artificial Intelligence (LISP, Prolog), Systems Programming (PL/S, BLISS, C), and Web Software (XHTML, JavaScript, PHP, Java, C#).
Language evaluation criteria include: clarity/simplicity/unity, orthogonality, support of abstraction (control and data), and safety.
Orthogonality in language design means every combination of features is meaningful, and independent functions should be controlled by independent mechanisms.
The document is authored by Dr. Nguyen Hua Phung and MEng. Tran Ngoc Bao Duy from the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, Ho Chi Minh University of Technology, VNU-HCM.
Fortran and MATLAB are examples of programming languages used for Scientific Applications.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Scientific Applications: Fortran, ALGOL 60, Julia, MATLAB.

key_facts.fact: LISP and Prolog are programming languages categorized under the Artificial Intelligence domain.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Artificial Intelligence: LISP, Prolog, ...

key_facts.fact: Imperative languages are the most dominant programming methodology due to the von Neumann computer architecture.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Imperative languages, most dominant, because of von Neumann computers.

key_facts.fact: A key advantage of an interpreter is its ability to provide better error diagnostics than a compiler.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: An interpreter, however, can usually give better error diagnostics than a compiler

key_facts.fact: The first phase of a compiler is called lexical analysis or scanning.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The first phase of a compiler is called lexical analysis or scanning.

key_facts.fact: The second phase of a compiler, which creates a syntax tree, is known as syntax analysis or parsing.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The second phase of the compiler is syntax analysis or parsing.

key_facts.fact: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

key_facts.fact: A schema is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Schema: a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application

key_facts.fact: Base tables are relations whose tuples are actually created and stored as a file by the DBMS.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Relation and its tuples are actually created and stored as a file by the DBMS.

key_facts.fact: The PRIMARY KEY clause specifies one or more attributes that make up the primary key of a relation.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: specifies one or more attributes that make up the primary key of a relation.

key_facts.fact: The ALTER command is used to change the definition of a base table or other named schema elements.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: ALTER command: change the definition of a base table or of other named schema elements

key_facts.verbatim_quote: SQL relation (table) is a multi-set (sometimes called a bag) of tuples; it is not a set of tuples

key_facts.fact: The GROUP BY clause forms groups of rows that have the same column value.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: GROUP BY : Forms groups of rows with same column value

key_facts.verbatim_quote: The HAVING-clause is used for specifying a selection condition on groups (rather than on individual tuples)

key_facts.fact: The DELETE command removes tuples from a relation.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Removes tuples from a relation

key_facts.fact: A view is a virtual table that is derived from other tables.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: A view is a “virtual” table that is derived from other tables

key_facts.fact: Searching algorithms are designed to check for or retrieve an element from a data structure, and are classified into two categories: Sequential Search and Interval Search.
Linear Search starts from the leftmost element of the list, compares the target x with each element one by one, returning the index if matched or -1 if no element matches.
Interval Search algorithms are specifically designed for searching in sorted data structures.
The hash table section covers basic concepts, direct-address tables, hash tables, hash functions, and open addressing as a collision-resolution technique.

The document is authored by Tran Ngoc Bao Duy from the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, Ho Chi Minh University of Technology, VNU-HCM, as Chapter 7 of a Data Structures and Algorithms course.
The time complexity of the Linear Search algorithm is O(n).
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The time complexity of the above algorithm is O(n).

key_facts.fact: Jump Search is a searching algorithm designed for sorted arrays.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Jump Search is a searching algorithm for sorted arrays.

key_facts.fact: In the worst case, the time complexity of Interpolation Search can be up to O(n).
key_facts.verbatim_quote: In worst case, it can take up to O(n).

key_facts.fact: The operations in a direct-address table, such as search and insert, take only O(1) time.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Each of these operations takes only O(1) time.

key_facts.fact: With hashing, an element with key k is stored in the slot designated by h(k).
key_facts.verbatim_quote: With hashing, this element is stored in slot h(k).

key_facts.fact: A collision in a hash table occurs when two keys hash to the same slot.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: two keys may hash to the same slot. We call this situation a collision.

key_facts.fact: In chaining, all elements that hash to the same slot are placed into the same linked list.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: In chaining, we place all the elements that hash to the same slot into the same linked list.

key_facts.fact: The hash function for the division method is defined as h(k) = k mod m.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: the hash function is h(k) = k mod m

documents.title: Introduction to Transaction Processing Concepts and Theory

key_facts.fact: A transaction is a logical unit of database processing that includes one or more access operations: read (retrieval), write (insert or update), and delete.
Transaction boundaries are defined by 'Begin Transaction' and 'End Transaction'; an application program may contain several transactions separated by these boundaries.
A single-user system allows at most one user at a time, while a multiuser system allows many users to access the system concurrently.
Concurrency can be implemented via interleaved processing (concurrent execution interleaved on a single CPU) or parallel processing (concurrent execution on multiple CPUs).

The basic database operations are read_item(X) - which finds the disk block containing X, copies it into a main-memory buffer, then copies X to a program variable - and write_item(X) - which writes the program variable's value back into the database item.
In a single-user system, a maximum of one user can utilize the system at any given time.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Single-User System: At most one user at a time can use the system.

key_facts.fact: A transaction is considered a logical unit of database processing, which encompasses one or more access operations.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: A Transaction: logical unit of database processing that includes one or more access operations

key_facts.fact: The Lost Update Problem occurs when two transactions access the same database items, leading to an incorrect item value.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: makes the value of some database item incorrect.

key_facts.fact: The Incorrect Summary Problem may arise when one transaction calculates an aggregate function while other transactions are updating the same records.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: one transaction is calculating an aggregate summary function on a number of records while other transactions are updating some of these records

key_facts.fact: Atomicity dictates that a transaction is an indivisible unit of work, which is either fully completed or not performed at all.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: A transaction is an atomic unit of processing; it is either performed in its entirety or not performed at all.

key_facts.fact: The system log, or journal, is responsible for tracking all transaction operations that modify the values of database items.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The log keeps track of all transaction operations that affect the values of database items.

key_facts.fact: The durability property ensures that once a transaction's changes are committed, they will not be lost due to a subsequent failure.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Once a transaction changes the database and the changes are committed, these changes must never be lost because of subsequent failure.

key_facts.fact: A schedule is classified as serial if all operations for every participating transaction are executed consecutively.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: A schedule S is serial if, for every transaction T participating in the schedule, all the operations of T are executed consecutively

key_facts.fact: Two schedules are considered conflict equivalent if the relative order of any two conflicting operations is the same in both.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Two schedules are said to be conflict equivalent if the order of any two conflicting operations is the same in both schedules.

key_facts.fact: The chapter covers: Connectivity (Paths and Circuits), Euler and Hamilton Paths, the Shortest Path Problem (Dijkstra's, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Ford's algorithm), and Graph Coloring.
A cut vertex (articulation point) is a vertex whose removal disconnects the graph; in Vietnamese: 'đỉnh cắt' hay 'điểm khớp'.
An Euler path is a path that traverses every edge of the graph exactly once; a Hamilton path visits every vertex exactly once.
Shortest path algorithms covered include Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford algorithm, and Floyd-Warshall algorithm.

The material is authored by Huynh Tuong Nguyen, Tran Tuan Anh, Nguyen An Khuong, and Le Hong Trang from the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Technology - VNUHCM, dated August 16, 2021.
A Hamilton circuit is defined as a circuit that visits each vertex in a graph exactly once.

Three rules of Hamilton Circuits are taught: (Rule 1) if deg(v) = 2, both edges incident to v must be used; (Rule 2) no subcircuit can be formed; (Rule 3) once two edges at a vertex v are determined, all other edges incident at v must be removed.
Property of Dijkstra's Algorithm: applicable for any graph G with any edge length ℓ(vi) ≥ 0, one-to-all shortest paths, time complexity O(|V|²).
Dijkstra's algorithm CAN be used on directed graphs (digraphs), but CANNOT be used on graphs with negative edge weights.

An application of Hamilton circuits is generating Gray Code: an n-digit Gray code can be generated by finding Hamilton circuits of an n-dimensional hypercube; Gray code is used in digital communication to reduce the effect of noise.
In a directed graph, a path is a sequence of ordered pairs representing directed edges.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Path is a sequence of (x0, x1), (x1, x2), . . . , (xn−1, xn)

key_facts.fact: In a connected undirected graph, a simple path exists between any two distinct vertices.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: There is a simple path between every pair of distinct vertices of a connected undirected graph.

key_facts.fact: A graph that does not have any cut vertices is called a nonseparable graph.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: This graph doesn't have cut vertices: nonseparable graph

key_facts.fact: Some slides in the document about Euler and Hamilton circuits were created by Chung Ki-hong and Hur Joon-seok from KAIST.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Some slides about Euler and Hamilton circuits are created by Chung Ki-hong and Hur Joon-seok from KAIST.

key_facts.fact: In Bayesian learning, all quantities of interest (parameters, hypotheses, predictions) are represented as probability distributions.

Bayesian learning is formulated as the manipulation of probabilities to evaluate and compare hypotheses; optimal decisions are derived by reasoning about posterior probabilities or expected utilities.
Each training example can incrementally update the hypothesis probability; combining prior knowledge with data yields the final posterior probability.

The Learning-Inference-Decision pipeline: Learning produces a posterior P(H|D) from prior P(H) and likelihood P(D|H); Inference computes the posterior predictive P(y|x,D); Decision selects the action a* = arg max_a E[U|a,D].

The chapter outline covers: Introduction, Bayes Rule, Parameter Estimation, Parameter Estimation Example, Priors in Bayesian Learning, and a Short Intro to Naive Bayes; authored by Thanh-Sach LE (ltsach@hcmut.edu.vn) at HCMUT, August 23, 2025.
In Bayesian Learning, learning is formulated as the manipulation of probabilities to evaluate and compare hypotheses.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Learning is formulated as the manipulation of probabilities to evaluate and compare hypotheses.

key_facts.fact: A prior distribution, denoted P(θ), expresses beliefs about parameters before any data is observed.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Prior distribution P(θ) expresses beliefs about parameters before observing data.

key_facts.fact: Conjugate priors are chosen so that the posterior distribution is in the same family as the prior, which simplifies computation.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: Conjugate priors: chosen so posterior is in the same family, simplifying computation.

key_facts.fact: In machine learning, using an L2 penalty on weights is equivalent to placing a Gaussian prior on those weights in a Bayesian framework.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: L2 penalty ∼ Gaussian prior on weights.

key_facts.fact: The Naive Bayes classifier is a form of MAP classification that relies on a conditional independence assumption among features.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: MAP classification with conditional independence assumption.

key_facts.fact: Per Tim Brown (President & CEO of IDEO), design thinking is a human-centered approach to innovation that integrates the needs of people, the possibilities of technology, and the requirements for business success.
The chapter outline covers: What is design thinking, Business Model Canvas, Hypothesis Testing for Value Creation, Prototyping, Information Architecture, and Fundamentals of Visual Design.
Hypothesis Testing for Value Creation consists of three components: a hypothesis statement, a test method, and a test metric & criteria.

Key phases of design thinking include Observing (study current market/users/competitors using qualitative and quantitative research), Ideating (discovery and creation), and Implementation (design experiments, test, iterate).

A Business Model (per David Teece) articulates the logic and provides data and other evidence demonstrating how a business creates and delivers value to customers; the Business Model Canvas is used to describe and design a value creation system.
Design thinking is a human-centered innovation approach integrating people's needs, technology's possibilities, and business requirements.

key_facts.verbatim_quote: Agile is a set of values and principles that guide how you should conduct innovation (from 2001)

key_facts.verbatim_quote: Gestalt (form, shape in German) is a group of visual perception principles developed by German psychologists in 1920s

key_facts.verbatim_quote: things that are close together appear to be more related than things that are spaced farther apart

key_facts.fact: The principle of closure suggests people tend to see a single, recognizable pattern in complex visual arrangements.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: we tend to look for a single, recognizable pattern

documents.title: Trường tĩnh điện trong chân không

key_facts.fact: Cường độ điện trường do điện tích điểm gây ra được xác định theo công thức E = k·q/r²·er (V/m hoặc N/C), trong đó k = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 9·10⁹ N·m²/C² và ε₀ ≈ 8,86·10⁻¹² C²/N·m².
Vecto E hướng ra xa q nếu q > 0, và hướng về phía q nếu q < 0; trong môi trường có hằng số điện môi tương đối ε > 1, cường độ điện trường giảm đi ε lần so với trong chân không.
Điện trường do hệ điện tích điểm gây ra bằng tổng vector cường độ điện trường do các điện tích trong hệ gây ra (nguyên lý chồng chất): E = ΣEᵢ.
Đường sức điện trường là những đường cong sao cho vecto E tiếp tuyến với nó tại mọi điểm; đường sức bắt đầu từ điện tích dương và kết thúc ở điện tích âm; đường sức điện trường tĩnh không khép kín.
Hai đường sức không bao giờ cắt nhau; nếu điện trường là điện trường đều thì các đường sức là những đường thẳng song song và cách đều nhau.

key_facts.fact: Demand is the ability and willingness to buy specific quantities of a good at alternative prices in a given time period, ceteris paribus.
Supply is the ability and willingness to sell (produce) specific quantities of a good at alternative prices in a given time period, ceteris paribus.
The law of demand states that the quantity of a good demanded in a given time period increases as its price falls, ceteris paribus.

The determinants of demand include: tastes (desire for this and other goods), income of the consumer, other goods (their availability and price), expectations (for income/prices/tastes), and the number of buyers.
A 'change in quantity demanded' refers to movements along a given demand curve in response to price changes of the good itself - distinct from a 'change in demand' which shifts the entire curve.
Demand is the ability and willingness to purchase specific quantities of a good at various prices within a given time, ceteris paribus.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The ability and willingness to buy specific quantities of a good at alternative prices in a given time period, ceteris paribus.

key_facts.fact: The law of demand states that the quantity of a good demanded increases as its price falls, assuming other factors remain constant.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The quantity of a good demanded in a given time period increases as its price falls, ceteris paribus.

key_facts.fact: The law of supply indicates that the quantity of a good supplied within a specific period rises as its price increases, ceteris paribus.
key_facts.verbatim_quote: The quantity of a good supplied in a given time period increases as its price increases, ceteris paribus.

key_facts.fact: The equilibrium price is the specific price point where the quantity supplied is equal to the quantity demanded.
